finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws. The result is discarded, so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any caller can wipe any tenant's data. export() uses checkRole(), which throws, so it is not affected.
finding.source: Any authenticated user, with no OWNER role, sends POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant id. The `tenant` and `u` arguments are passed to wipe().
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive tenant data wipe (Admin.java:27)

trace.note: requireRole() returns u.roles().contains(role). The javadoc says it does not throw, but the name suggests it enforces the role.
wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called as a bare statement. The boolean result is ignored, so execution always continues.

finding.guards_checked: The only guard on the path is the requireRole call at line 26, which has no effect. checkRole at line 18 does throw, but wipe() does not use it. I found no other middleware, annotation or check in the repo; src/Admin.java is the only source file. Tenant scoping is also absent: roles are global and User has no tenant field.
